record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For positive integers s and t, let g(s,t) be the least minimum-degree threshold such that every graph with minimum degree at least g(s,t) can be partitioned into S and T with delta(G[S]) at least s and delta(G[T]) at least t. On triangle-free graphs, is the sharp threshold g(s,t) equal to s + t?

evidence.quote: He showed essentially that for positive integers s and t, there is an integer g(s, t) such that the vertex set of every graph G with minimum degree at least g(s, t) can be partitioned into S and T which induce subgraphs of minimum degree at least s and t, respectively
Then Stiebitz asked a question: is it true that, for any positive integers s and t, g(s, t) = s + t on triangle-free graphs?
With the same technique of Stiebitz, Kaneko[35] answered the question affirmatively and proved that if s ≥ 1 and t ≥ 1, then g(s, t) ≤ s + t on triangle-free graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For positive integers $s$ and $t$, define $g(s,t)$ to be the least integer with the following property: every finite simple graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G) \geq g(s,t)$ admits a partition of its vertex set $V(G) = S \sqcup T$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ has minimum degree at least $s$ and the induced subgraph $G[T]$ has minimum degree at least $t$. Restricting attention to the class of triangle-free graphs, prove or disprove that $g(s,t) = s+t$ for all positive integers $s,t$. Equivalently, show that every triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least $s+t$ admits such a partition, and that this bound is sharp.
artifact.status_search_result: Kaneko (1998) proved that for triangle-free graphs and any positive integers s,t, every graph with minimum degree at least s+t admits the required partition, settling Stiebitz's question affirmatively. The lower bound s+t is easily seen to be tight, so g(s,t) = s+t on triangle-free graphs.

status_evidence.title: Kaneko, On decomposition of triangle-free graphs under degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: It is shown that if G is a triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least s+t, then V(G) can be partitioned into S and T with delta(G[S]) >= s and delta(G[T]) >= t.
status_evidence.claim: Kaneko proved g(s,t) <= s+t on triangle-free graphs, answering Stiebitz's question.
